newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Wools of NZ invests NZ$4 mln in WRONZ expansion.
newsitem.headline: Wools of NZ invests NZ$4 mln in WRONZ expansion.

text.p: Wools of New Zealand on Wednesday said it had invested NZ$4 million in an expansion of the Wool Research Organisation of New Zealand (WRONZ).
The new "Growers' Wing" of the WRONZ laboratories at Lincoln was officially opened by Prime Minister Jim Bolger.
Retiring chairman Pat Morrison said research and development was fundamental to underpin the success of the Fernmark Value System.

"Woolgrowers have made a $4 million investment in new WRONZ laboratories through Wools of New Zealand. So we can see how important wool research and product development is to our strategy and to the future of the sheep industry in New Zealand," Morrison said in a statement.
Since 1991, wool growers had increased their annual funding of WRONZ by more than 80 percent.
In the current year, Wools of NZ investment in WRONZ programmes would reach a new high of $5.1 million, as well as the $4 million grant already made to fund the new wing.
"The expansion of WRONZ facilities will enable us to step up our research and development of uniquely New Zealand apparel technologies and products," Morrison said.
He paid tribute to government contributions and industry funding of wool research. "I expect industry this year to provide funding of about $5.6 million, up 230 percent in the past five years."
